faq.q: Can I make a YouTube Shorts ad from one product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one clear photo, share your idea in one sentence and pick 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. The credit cost shows before you start.

faq.q: How long should a Shorts ad be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Six seconds suits one product moment, while a longer clip gives a demo room to finish.

faq.q: Do I need to book a creator or film anything?
faq.a: No. The Short is built from your own product photo, so there is no shoot day and no wait for footage. Run another job when you need a new angle.

faq.q: Does the Short include music and captions?
faq.a: No. Add a soundtrack and caption text in YouTube or an editor after download. The file itself has no soundtrack or words.

faq.q: Can I run the same file as a TikTok ad?
faq.a: Yes. A 9:16 file fits both feeds, but preview it in each player so the buttons do not cover the product.
Use a sharp photo that shows the whole product and the part that moves, with a little space around it for the player controls.

faq.q: When do I need a 16:9 video?
faq.a: Use 16:9 for a regular YouTube video or in-stream ad. That is a separate wide job and is not a Shorts format.

faq.q: Can I use the Short in a paid campaign?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark and is yours to run through Google Ads, subject to Google's current ad review rules.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded steamer photo as the product reference and preserve its shape and color. In a bright laundry room, adult hands press the white garment steamer once across a wrinkled blue shirt sleeve; the cloth smooths as steam passes. Close side view with one continuous slow push-in and the steamer centered. Natural window light and realistic fabric texture. End with the steamer clear and still in frame. Sound: soft steam hiss and room tone; no music, captions or on-screen text.
